drafts.title: Keep the driving feel: preserve strong acceleration and smooth, responsive power delivery
drafts.description: Customer experiences a consistently strong, smooth and satisfying acceleration with linear, predictable power delivery across drive modes so everyday driving feels powerful yet refined.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In mixed driving validation (city+highway with normal load) 95% of test drives report no perceptible surges, jerks, or delayed responses during acceleration and measured 0–60 mph time remains within ±10% of target benchmark for the model variant.
assumptions: Powertrain hardware in the successor will be refined but broadly similar in class to today's systems; software controls can substantially improve throttle mapping and blending.
Benchmark 0–60 mph targets will be set per variant by product team; ±10% allows for realistic tuning trade-offs.
uncertainties: Actual achievable improvements depend on final powertrain architecture and constraints from emissions/efficiency or packaging.
Customer perception testing can be subjective; resolving edge cases (e.g., cold starts, transitions to ICE in PHEV) may require multiple iterations.

drafts.title: Maintain ride comfort and planted handling that feel both luxurious and sporty
drafts.description: Customers experience a smooth, quiet, and comfortable ride for daily driving and long trips while retaining confident, sporty handling and responsiveness when desired.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In standardized ride and handling tests, subjective comfort ratings from a representative user panel reach at least 4 out of 5 for long‑distance comfort and handling stability; road noise (dB) and vibration metrics must not be worse than the current G60 baseline by more than 5%.
assumptions: Chassis and NVH improvements are feasible within successor vehicle weight and cost targets.
A representative user panel and objective NVH test procedures will be used to compare to current model.
uncertainties: Trade-offs between sportiness and ultimate comfort may require mode‑based tuning; some customers will prefer firmer or softer setups.

drafts.title: Driver seat: provide a higher and more adjustable seating range so shorter drivers have clear forward visibility
drafts.description: Shorter drivers can raise the driver seat high enough and adjust seating geometry easily so they have an unobstructed, comfortable view over the hood and instrument/passenger bar without compromising support.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In an ergonomic validation with participants down to 152 cm (5th percentile female), 95% of participants achieve the required forward sightline over the hood and report a comfortable seating position in <=3 adjustments; repeated tests show consistent results across body types.
assumptions: Seat mechanism adjustments can be extended within packaging limits of the successor model.
The sightline target will be defined by the ergonomics team based on typical hood geometry.
uncertainties: Packaging or cost constraints could limit absolute travel; some extreme body shapes may still need additional adjustments.

drafts.title: Make essential climate, odometer and common controls discoverable and operable quickly
drafts.description: Customers can find and operate essential controls (climate fan/temperature, vent direction, seat heating, odometer/trip mileage and quick defog) without navigating deep menus or taking their eyes off the road.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In usability testing, 95% of participants can access and complete each essential task within 2 taps or voice command and in under 5 seconds while driving in a simulator; identified control locations/settings are reachable within 2 menu levels if not on the main view.
assumptions: A combination of UI changes, physical shortcuts, and improved voice commands will be used to meet timing goals.
Driver simulator tests adequately approximate in-vehicle performance.
uncertainties: Some customers will still prefer physical knobs; balancing full digital design with quick access may require hybrid controls.

drafts.title: Large central display: keep the prominent long touchscreen but reduce distraction and smear
drafts.description: Customers enjoy a visually striking long touchscreen that remains readable in bright light, smudges less, and does not require excessive menu navigation for frequent tasks.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In controlled light tests the display remains readable (legibility test score >=90% for common UI elements) under direct sunlight simulation; in a 30‑user fingerprint visibility test, 90% of users rate smudge visibility as low or very low after typical daily use.
assumptions: Improvements will come from UI design, anti-reflective treatments and oleophobic coatings that are durable for at least 24 months.
User perception tests accurately reflect real-world viewing conditions.
uncertainties: Coating durability and trade-offs with touchscreen responsiveness may limit performance; extreme bright-light conditions can still reduce legibility.

drafts.title: Apple CarPlay and phone connectivity: make wireless CarPlay reliable and seamless
drafts.description: Customers can connect their phones via Apple CarPlay reliably and maintain a stable connection for the duration of typical drives without frequent re-pairing or audio dropouts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In field tests across a representative set of phone models, a wireless CarPlay connection is established within 10 seconds on 95% of attempts and remains connected for at least 99% of the duration of 2‑hour test drives without user intervention.
assumptions: Improvements will be achieved through software/firmware updates and stronger interoperability testing with phone vendors.
Representative phone set will include top 20 phone models in the target market.
uncertainties: Ongoing changes to phone OS updates and third‑party app behavior may affect long‑term reliability.

drafts.title: Wireless charging: phone fits reliably and charges without frequent repositioning
drafts.description: Customers can place a common smartphone on the in‑car wireless charging surface and expect it to begin and continue charging without repositioning or intermittent stops.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In bench tests with the top 20 phone models by market share, 95% begin wireless charging within 5 seconds of placement and maintain continuous charging for 95% of a 60‑minute idle period without requiring repositioning; the pad accommodates phones up to 85 mm wide without edge lift.
assumptions: Qi wireless charging standards and phone form factors remain similar over the next 3–5 years.
Compatibility matrix will be maintained and tested against popular phone sizes and cases.
uncertainties: Proprietary phone cases, MagSafe accessories or future phone designs could reduce compatibility.
Charging speed will vary by phone model; target focuses on reliability rather than absolute wattage.

drafts.title: Hands‑free trunk: make touchless kick-to-open robust and predictable
drafts.description: When customers use the touchless kick-to-open gesture with hands full, the trunk opens reliably on the first attempt and does not open unexpectedly.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In field testing across typical gait patterns and footwear, the kick-to-open action triggers trunk open within 1.5 seconds on the first valid attempt in at least 95% of trials and false‑positive openings occur in fewer than 0.5% of parked‑vehicle tests.
assumptions: Improved sensor algorithms and calibration can reduce false negatives/positives.
Testing includes varied user heights, footwear and motion speeds representative of owners.
uncertainties: Extreme occlusions (e.g., obstructed sensors), heavy rain or frozen sensors could still cause failures.

drafts.title: Door unlock behavior: default to unlock all doors and make setting easy to change
drafts.description: When customers approach with the key, all passenger doors unlock by default (configurable), and the setting to change this behavior is discoverable and reversible in under two taps.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Default unlock behavior unlocks all doors in 99% of proximity unlock events in field testing; changing the unlock setting is discoverable in the infotainment or phone app in ≤2 taps and persists across vehicle restarts for 100% of test cases.
assumptions: Comfort Access and key-proximity hardware remain functionally similar and settings persistence is feasible in software.
Default behavior can be set centrally by product policy.
uncertainties: Some markets or fleet use cases may require single-door unlock as default; behavior should remain configurable.

drafts.title: Allow drivers to permanently disable auto start‑stop easily
drafts.description: Customers can turn off the automatic engine start‑stop function and have that preference remembered so they are not forced to re-disable it on every drive.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A clearly labeled setting or physical control to disable start‑stop is discoverable in ≤3 taps and the off preference persists across vehicle restarts for 100% of tested vehicles; usability test shows 95% of participants can find and set it within 30 seconds.
assumptions: Software control over start‑stop logic and user preference memory is permitted by system architecture.
If regulations require start‑stop, the persistent user preference will operate within allowed constraints.
uncertainties: Regulatory or emissions rules in certain markets might limit the ability to permanently disable start‑stop.

drafts.title: Brake quality: eliminate early squeal, grinding and excessive dust
drafts.description: Customers experience brakes that stop smoothly without unpleasant squeal or grabbing and that do not create excessive visible brake dust shortly after ownership.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Quality monitoring shows fewer than 2% of vehicles report squeal/grinding or excessive dust complaints within the first 6 months; road tests under typical driving produce no squeal louder than 55 dBA during routine braking events.
assumptions: Material selection, bedding-in procedures and calibration improvements can materially reduce noise and dust.
dBA threshold for perceptible squeal is set based on prior studies and will be validated in acoustic labs.
uncertainties: Brake noise can be sensitive to environmental conditions, wheel/tire combinations and driver behavior; absolute elimination is unlikely.

drafts.title: Range display and real‑world range consistency: reduce surprise and anxiety
drafts.description: Customers see a realistic and consistent range estimate that reflects real-world conditions so they can reliably plan commutes and trips without unexpected shortfalls.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In mixed real-world driving tests (including cold-weather runs), displayed remaining electric range error is within ±5% of measured real-world range for at least 90% of test drives; sudden range jumps (changes >5% within 5 minutes without driving condition change) occur in fewer than 1% of drives.
assumptions: Successor vehicle will use improved range estimation algorithms leveraging more vehicle and environmental inputs.
Testing will include representative cold-weather scenarios and mixed urban/highway cycles.
uncertainties: Extreme climatic variations and charging state histories can still cause discrepancies; educating customers about conditions may be needed.

drafts.title: Highway assistant: retain and improve reliability for relaxed highway driving
drafts.description: Customers can rely on the highway assistant to reduce workload and provide smooth hands-free driving on supported highways with predictable handover behavior.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On eligible highway segments, the system can engage and maintain hands-free assisted driving for at least 95% of the time without unexpected disengagements; when handover is required, the system provides clear and timely alerts and driver takeover occurs safely within defined seconds in 99% of events.
assumptions: Maps, sensors and software stacks will be enhanced to support broader coverage and higher reliability.
Driver monitoring and handover timing criteria will be defined by the assistance product team.
uncertainties: Regulatory changes to hands-free driving may alter available functionality in some markets.

drafts.title: Provide stable in-vehicle connectivity: reliable WiFi hotspot for common use
drafts.description: Customers can use the car's WiFi hotspot for typical passenger needs (streaming, navigation updates, basic browsing) with stable throughput in urban/suburban conditions.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In urban/suburban network tests, the vehicle hotspot sustains median downstream throughput ≥10 Mbps per active user and maintains a connection success rate of 98% across trips of up to 2 hours.
assumptions: Carrier agreements and hardware modems equivalent to current generations will be available in the successor timeframe.
Throughput target supports common passenger needs but higher performance may require external tethering.
uncertainties: Cellular network coverage and carrier throttling will significantly affect real-world performance in rural or congested areas.

drafts.title: Voice control: improve recognition for common vehicle tasks
drafts.description: Customers can use voice commands to perform common tasks (climate, navigation destination entry, phone calls, media) with high recognition accuracy so voice is a realistic alternative while driving.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In controlled and noisy in-vehicle tests, voice recognition succeeds (correct intent executed) on at least 90% of utterances for a predefined set of common tasks and handles natural phrasing for at least 80% of users in the test panel.
assumptions: Speech models can be updated over-the-air and local/noisy-environment robustness will improve with better microphones and models.
Common task set will be defined and localized per market.
uncertainties: Accent, background noise and third‑party app behavior may reduce accuracy for some users.

drafts.title: Out-of-scope (engineering spec): Specify wireless charging pad power and physical mounting details
drafts.description: Engineering-level specification for wireless charger power output (watts), coil placement and tray dimensions to support fast charging and phone fit.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: N/A — engineering specification to be defined by HW team (e.g., X W output, tray width Y mm).
assumptions: Customers asked for more reliable wireless charging and correct sizing; exact power and mechanical specs are an engineering decision.
uncertainties: Specifying exact wattage or coil count is an engineering choice and may change with phone standards.
drafts.scope_reason: This draft is an engineering specification (power/output/physical dimensions) rather than a direct customer-facing outcome; engineering teams should convert customer outcome requirements into these specs.
